title: Legacy Archive Synthesis for Legal Discovery
business: A global law firm managing decades of unstructured litigation archives.
problem: The firm faces high costs and latency when manually indexing millions of pages of historical case files, leading to inefficient discovery processes and missed connections between legacy documents.
solution: By leveraging the 1M token context window of Claude Opus 5, the firm can ingest entire case archives into a single prompt session to perform cross-document thematic analysis, identifying patterns that smaller context models would miss.
steps: Aggregate historical case documents into a unified, token-optimized dataset.
Utilize the Claude API with the claude-opus-5 model ID to process the 1M token context.
Apply prompt caching to the core legal framework and document structure to reduce recurring input costs.
Execute thematic extraction queries to map relationships across the entire archive.
Review synthesis outputs for legal accuracy and relevance to current discovery requirements.
outcome: The firm achieves a comprehensive, unified view of historical case data, significantly accelerating the discovery phase without needing to manually cross-reference individual document silos.
limitation: Claude Opus 5 is a legacy model; while it supports a large context window, its knowledge cutoff is May 2026, which may exclude recent legal precedents or regulatory changes. To check for relevance, developers should compare synthesis outputs against a secondary verification set of post-May 2026 documents.
